question: In patients with rotator cuff tears, is cellular therapy (e.g. mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow aspirate, platelet-rich plasma) beneficial compared with controls for healing and clinical outcomes?
eligibility: Patients with a rotator cuff tear (partial- or full-thickness) or undergoing rotator cuff repair.
The intervention delivers a cellular therapy (MSCs, bone marrow aspirate concentrate, PRP, adipose- or tendon-derived cells) as biologic augmentation.
Comparison against a control or standard repair without cellular augmentation.
Reports a healing/retear, pain, or functional outcome.
A randomized or otherwise comparative clinical study in humans.
as_of_source: day after the latest Entrez date among gold records (a lower bound on the review's search date)
source: SYNERGY dataset Muthu_2022; 'Is cellular therapy beneficial in management of rotator cuff tears?' (World J Meta-Anal 2022, doi:10.13105/wjma.v10.i3.162); gold = label_included==1 rows with DOI via [AID]
notes: Converted from the protocol-first branch. naive_blocks come from protocols written by the fixture author, some tightened while looking at the gold set, so the naive floor may be optimistic.
